evidence.excerpt:
Autonomous research agents are increasingly
used to automate large portions of scientific re-
search, yet they are prone to research integrity
violations (RIVs): behaviors that compromise
the validity, reproducibility, or faithfulness of
the research process. We present RIDAR, a
framework for automated RIV detection and
runtime intervention. First, we introduce RIVT,
a comprehensive taxonomy of 14 RIV types
spanning the full research lifecycle. Build-
ing on RIVT, we present RIDAR-POST-HOC,
a framework to detect RIVs within agent tra-
jectories. RIDAR-POST-HOCachieves 85.2%
F1 performance on RIV-GOLD, a benchmark
for RIV detection with 60 expert-annotated
trajectories. Applying RIDAR-POST-HOCto
RIV-WILD, a dataset of 300 agent trajecto-
ries across 50 distinct research tasks, we de-
tect 3,964 RIV instances in 99.7% of trajec-
tories, revealing the prevalence of RIVs in
current agents.

evidence.excerpt:
of RIVs in autonomous research agents,
we construct RIV-WILD, a dataset of 300 agent
trajectories collected from 6 frontier harness-model
configurations across 50 distinct research tasks.
RIDAR-POST-HOCidentifies 3,964 RIV instances
across 99.7% of these trajectories, with analysis re-
vealing how violation patterns vary across task and
RIV types. Finally, to test whether RIVs can be mit-
igated through runtime intervention, we construct
RIV-LIVE, a 60-trajectory subset of RIV-WILD
re-run with RIDAR-RUNTIMEintervention, each
paired with its non-intervened baseline. RIDAR-
RUNTIMEreduces the mean number of RIVs re-
maining at task completion from 14.9 to 9.4, yield-
ing a 36.8% decrease. These results show that
RIVs are widespread in current autonomous re-
search agents and that automated runtime interven-
tion offers an effective safeguard.

Detecting RIVs in long agent trajectories poses
a core tension: detection must achieve compre-
hensive coverage while avoiding false positives.
RIDAR-POST-HOCresolves this tension by explic-
itly separating candidate proposal from validation:
an Analyzer agent searches the full trajectory com-
prehensively to propose evidence-grounded RIV
candidates, while a Verifier agent independently
determines which candidates are sufficiently sup-
ported. We assign different LLM backbones to the
two agents to prevent self-preference biases (Pan-
ickssery et al., 2024; Goel et al., 2025).
During detection, the Analyzer audits the
full trajectory segment by segment under an
audit schema, which organizes auditing around a
reference notebook and a group of rubrics. For
each segment, the Analyzer updates the reference
notebook R with three types of observed facts Tref:
task goals, constraints, and

evidence.excerpt:
A finding that arrives after a run has ended can
document a violation but cannot correct it. We
therefore extend RIV detection to enable runtime
intervention before a run completes. To ensure in-
tervention timeliness, RIDAR-RUNTIMEemploys
a single resident Analyzer agent paired with a rule-
based Supervisor. The Analyzer processes growing
agent trajectories in windows and follows the same
audit schema as RIDAR-POST-HOC, maintaining
a notebook R and identified objects under Taudit.
Once an RIV becomes decidable based on accumu-
lated evidence, the Analyzer outputs a live finding
vt = (bt, kt, Et), where t denotes the trajectory
prefix at detection. To keep pace with the acting
agent, the Analyzer may delegate time-consuming
evidence collection tasks to background subagents
while retaining the final judgment itself. Each live
finding is passed to the Supervisor, which delivers
targeted

research tasks for RIV analysis, RIV-GOLDpro-
vides agent trajectories with expert RIV annota-

accuracy additionally reported at the
taxonomy level.
As shown in Table 2, RIDAR-POST-HOCwith
the default configuration achieves an instance-level
F1 of 85.2%, at 87.1% precision and 83.3% recall.
Requiring the matched findings to share the same
RIVT type reduces F1 by 12.7 points, whereas
taxonomy-level F1 remains 86.7%. These pat-
terns suggest that RIDAR-POST-HOCidentifies
the right violations and correctly judges which vio-
lation types occur in each trajectory, but sometimes
assigns a different type than the annotators to an
individual finding. One contributing factor isunder-
segmentation, where RIDAR-POST-HOCreports
several separately annotated violations as one find-
ing. Since each finding carries only a single RIVT
type, it can agree in type with at most one of the
gold human annotations.

To understand why some violations persist after
runtime intervention, we focus on the 8 of 60
matched pairs in which the intervention trajec-
tory contains more accepted findings than its non-
intervened baseline. Across these reverse-increase
pairs, we analyze all 67 findings remaining in the
intervention trajectories and group their causes
into three categories. (1)Detection gaps (85.1%).
Some violations identified by RIDAR-POST-HOC
are not detected by RIDAR-RUNTIME. These de-
tection gaps mainly arise for two reasons. First,
to ensure timely intervention, RIDAR-RUNTIME
uses only an Analyzer, while RIDAR-POST-HOC
has an additional Verifier to review and refine can-
didate findings. Second, RIDAR-RUNTIMEpro-
cesses trajectories incrementally, whereas some vi-
olations become apparent only from reviewing the
complete trajectory. These detection gaps make
RIDAR-RUNTIMEless comprehensive

evidence.excerpt:
This work has several limitations. First, RIDAR
relies on LLM-based judgments. Although RI-
DAR achieves high agreement with human anno-
tations on RIV-GOLD, its performance may still
vary across backbone LLMs, research tasks, and
trajectory records. Human review therefore re-
mains necessary in high-stakes settings. Second,
the evaluation of RIDAR in this paper primarily
covers research tasks from domains of mathematics
and machine learning. We leave a broader evalua-
tion across other scientific domains to future work.
Finally, we study frontier general-purpose agent
harnesses because they are increasingly used by
researchers worldwide to assist and automate sci-
entific research, making their research integrity a
pressing concern. Our trajectories do not cover spe-
cialized research agent frameworks, and whether
the same patterns hold in such systems remains an
open question.

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Human expert annotations on 60 disjoint-task trajectories corroborate the detector, yielding 85.2% instance-level F1 and 87.1% precision, with ablations showing each component contributes to this agreement [E3551b39bec139607-B0038, E3551b39bec139607-B0040, E3551b39bec139607-B0041].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline detection performance is established against 17 human expert annotations on RIV-GOLD, with bidirectional matching performed by a separate Claude-Sonnet-5.5 judge [E3551b39bec139607-B0010, E3551b39bec139607-B0031, E3551b39bec139607-B0038].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The RIDAR detector is configured through prompt engineering, a fixed audit rubric, and rule-based middleware, with backbone choices (GLM-5.3 Analyzer, GPT-5.6-Sol Verifier) selected without reported iterative tuning against the evaluation benchmark [E3551b39bec139607-B0016, E3551b39bec139607-B0018, E3551b39bec139607-B0033].

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding detector precision/recall, the widespread nature of reporting violations in current autonomous agents, and the effectiveness of runtime interventions are well-aligned with tabular results, ablation experiments, and detailed error analyses [E3551b39bec139607-B0034, E3551b39bec139607-B0040, E3551b39bec139607-B0044].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is evaluated on RIV-GOLD (60 trajectories annotated by 17 human experts), achieving 85.2% instance-level F1 and 86.7% taxonomy F1 matched via an independent judge, evaluated on 300 diverse agent trajectories in RIV-WILD, and tested in a matched 60-trajectory live trial (RIV-LIVE) where runtime interventions reduced remaining violations by 36.8% [E3551b39bec139607-B0002, E3551b39bec139607-B0031, E3551b39bec139607-B0037, E3551b39bec139607-B0038, E3551b39bec139607-B0040].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: 17 independent human expert annotations on the RIV-GOLD dataset validate the detector's findings, showing 85.2% instance-level F1 and 87.1% precision [E3551b39bec139607-B0010, E3551b39bec139607-B0038, E3551b39bec139607-B0040].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Independent human expert annotations across 60 benchmark trajectories on disjoint tasks, mapped bidirectionally using a separate model (Claude-Sonnet-5.5) as an LLM judge [E3551b39bec139607-B0010, E3551b39bec139607-B0031, E3551b39bec139607-B0038].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: System prompt engineering, structured rubrics, and heuristic completion/barrier rules configured for the Analyzer (GLM-5.3) and Verifier (GPT-5.6-Sol) without iterative parametric training against the test benchmark [E3551b39bec139607-B0016, E3551b39bec139607-B0018, E3551b39bec139607-B0033].

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge limitations, including dependence on LLM judgments, potential under-segmentation of complex violations, restriction of tasks primarily to ML and mathematics, and focusing on general-purpose harnesses rather than specialized monolithic agent systems [E3551b39bec139607-B0039, E3551b39bec139607-B0051].
primary.method_assessment: RIDAR-POST-HOC divides audit proposal and verification between different LLM backbones (GLM-5.3 Analyzer and GPT-5.6-Sol Verifier) coordinated by a deterministic rule-based middleware, while RIDAR-RUNTIME operates on prefix windows with a completion barrier [E3551b39bec139607-B0016, E3551b39bec139607-B0024, E3551b39bec139607-B0033]. The architecture, audit schemas, and prompt designs are comprehensively documented [E3551b39bec139607-B0017, E3551b39bec139607-B0024, E3551b39bec139607-B0110, E3551b39bec139607-B0117].
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-scoped investigation of research integrity failures in AI research agents with clear taxonomic definitions, reproducible methodology, robust expert-annotated gold evaluation, and ablation studies confirming each system component's role.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces RIVT, a 14-category taxonomy of research integrity violations across the scientific workflow, alongside RIDAR: a dual-agent post-hoc detector (RIDAR-POST-HOC) and an incremental runtime monitoring and intervention framework (RIDAR-RUNTIME) for autonomous LLM research agents [E3551b39bec139607-B0002, E3551b39bec139607-B0009, E3551b39bec139607-B0010].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-scoped investigation of research integrity failures in AI research agents with clear taxonomic definitions, reproducible methodology, robust expert-annotated gold evaluation, and ablation studies confirming each system component's role.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly acknowledge limitations, including dependence on LLM judgments, potential under-segmentation of complex violations, restriction of tasks primarily to ML and mathematics, and focusing on general-purpose harnesses rather than specialized monolithic agent systems [E3551b39bec139607-B0039, E3551b39bec139607-B0051].

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.

relation_to_agentic_memory.value: Studies agents that perform or evaluate multi-step research workflows

research_relevance.value: Directly relevant to autonomous/deep research workflows based on screening evidence.
